A.explanation: Both forces $F$ act vertically downwards, so they are parallel but in the same direction and give a non-zero resultant force.

B.explanation: The left force acts down and the right force acts diagonally up, so the forces are not parallel and not equal and opposite.

C.explanation: One force $F$ acts down and the other acts to the right, so the forces are perpendicular and cannot cancel to zero resultant.

D.explanation: One force $F$ acts up at the left end and the other $F$ acts down at the right end, so they are equal, opposite and parallel with zero resultant but a turning moment.

hints: Notice the direction of each $F$ arrow on the rod ends - check whether the two arrows point in the same direction, perpendicular directions, or opposite directions.
Recall a couple needs two forces that are equal in size $F$, parallel to each other, and opposite in sense so the vector sum is zero.
Compare the turning effect about the centre: only opposite parallel forces both tend to turn the rod the same way without a net push.
walkthrough: Look at what is given: a horizontal rod with two forces, each labelled $F$, applied at the ends in diagrams A to D.
State the rule for a couple: two forces must satisfy $F_{net} = F - F = 0$, so they must be equal in magnitude, parallel in line of action, and opposite in direction.
Check A, B and C: A has two parallel downward forces, B has downward and diagonal forces, and C has downward and horizontal forces, so none has equal and opposite parallel forces.

Check the remaining diagram: one $F$ upward at the left end and one $F$ downward at the right end are parallel, equal and opposite, giving zero resultant but a resultant moment $moment = F \times separation$.
Therefore the equal and opposite parallel pair is the couple. This is option D
